correctness.rationale: The exact finite n Curie–Weiss magnetization sector sum yields ground-state normalized F=cos(nx)+n q cos((n−2)x)+C(n,2)u cos((n−4)x)+o(u), q=e^(−2(n−1)β/n), u=e^(−4(n−2)β/n), for fixed n≥5. At θ=(2k−1)π/(2n), derivative −n(−1)^(k−1) is nonzero and trigonometric identities give first shift q sin2θ and second C(n,2)/n u sin4θ=(n−1)u sin4θ/2. Since q²/u=e^(−4β/n)→0, quadratic first-sector corrections are asymptotically smaller. For n=4, the j=2 zero-magnetization sector appears only once, yielding 3/4 instead of paired (n−1)/2. For n=3, Taylor expansion of cos3x+3e^(−4β/3)cos x=0 gives √3/2 q−√3/4 q²+O(q³); for n=2 exact equation cos2x=−e^(-β) gives 1/2 e^(-β)+O(e^(-3β)). Hou–Jiang–Newman Theorem 2 establishes simplicity/ordering of the moving roots so the local IFT expansions exhaust indexed principal roots. Independent 70-digit direct partition-sum root solves for n=2–6 corroborated first coefficients; fixed-n asymptotic proof does not rely on those samples.
